avoid_for: Quiet luxury or premium brand presentations, long-form reading experiences, dark-mode-first products, or restrained minimal SaaS where loud confetti and 244px type would feel noisy — color here is punctuation, not decoration to add casually.
best_for: Fintech / trading / devtool marketing pages that want a confident, maximalist editorial manifesto register — poster-scale grotesque headlines on a light ash canvas with Bauhaus color blocks, Stripe/Replit-adjacent.
name: Composer
palette_voice: Light ash Concrete (#e5e7eb) canvas with Paper (#ffffff) cards and hairline Concrete borders everywhere; black Obsidian (#000000) text on near-white is the 21:1 safety floor; a confetti of vivid rectangles (Signal Blue #1871da, Pulse Green #1ec072, Hot Pink #f6609f, Solar Yellow #ffbb38, Cotton Candy #ffb4ed) is pure decoration — never the CTA, which is always the filled black pill; blue-tinted shadow (rgba(24,113,218,0.25)) instead of neutral gray; max three chromatic accents per composition.
signature_moves: 244px display headline at weight 600, line-height 1.0, positive tracking — transforms headings into posters, paired with a smaller 'headline + dek' subtitle
Confetti color blocks — zero-radius solid rectangles (40-200px) scattered across the gray canvas as geometric information, not decoration
Filled black pill CTA (Obsidian fill, white text, 9999px radius, arrow glyph) — the system's only filled button, never chromatic
Cotton Candy (#ffb4ed) marker-pen highlight on key words in body copy for editorial scannability without changing text color
Sharp-vs-pill geometric tension — 2px icon containers and 6px cards alongside 9999px pill buttons

source.shadow: blue-tinted subtle rgba(24,113,218,0.25) 0 1px 2px 0 + multi-layer soft card shadows

typographic_voice: One geometric grotesque (Neue Haas Grotesk Display, subst. Inter) spans 244px poster headlines to 14px nav with positive tracking (0.01-0.057em) at every size for editorial breathing room; Inter takes over for compact UI chrome below 16px; the 244px weight-600 hero is the signature 'headline as magazine cover' — no condensed faces, no negative letter-spacing.
